tier_reason: arXiv preprint (no venue stated) by the authors (UNICAMP); compares against OpenBLAS, BLIS, MKL, oneDNN, FlashGEMM on named CPUs, but no LP-GEMM code is released and compiler/flags are not stated. Tier stays C; the claim was overstated, so the verdict is downgrade.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Average 2.25x over OpenBLAS for sequential (chained) GEMMs on Intel Xeon Gold 6252 (AVX-512), single-thread; single-GEMM median ~1.5x over OpenBLAS. Abstract claims 'up to 2x for x86 and up to 5x for RISC-V for Attention-like workloads', but the RISC-V attention figure (Fig. 6b) shows roughly 1.5x at best.
corrections.caveats: No LP-GEMM code released (the only linked repo, czariv/simple_attention, is a 0-star Llama attention driver without the GEMM kernels); compiler and flags unstated; kernels derived from OpenBLAS and the gain comes mainly from skipping packing; BLIS and FlashGEMM median speedups exceed the initial LP-GEMM kernel on single GEMMs; the 5x RISC-V abstract figure is not borne out by the paper's own plots.

notes: Real result, but the headline is narrow: 2.25x average holds only for chained GEMMs against OpenBLAS. Record the shortcoming that the abstract's 5x RISC-V claim is inconsistent with Fig. 6b. Usability stays reference (no code).

tier_reason: arXiv preprint by the authors (NUDT, 'Demystifying ARM SME to Optimize General Matrix Multiplications') with averages vs OpenBLAS 5.7x, Accelerate 1.23x, LIBXSMM 3.96x, KleidiAI 4.69x on an Apple M4 Pro with AppleClang 16; it is called open-source but gives no code URL and no flags, and no venue is stated, so it is not A or B.

corrections.caveats: Paper calls MpGEMM open-source but links no code (none found); flags unstated; OpenBLAS lacked SME kernels on M4 at the time, which inflates the 5.7x figure, so the meaningful win is 1.23x over Apple Accelerate. An independent MIT reimplementation of the paper's design (github.com/tesch1/MTGEMM-A, Apple clang 21, -O3 -march=armv8.6-a+sme2, bench/bench.cpp) measured the paper design at 1.09x over Accelerate fp32 single-thread geomean, and its own tuned version at 1.25x.

notes: Numbers match the page. Lead: tesch1/MTGEMM-A (MIT, 0 stars, active Sep 2026) is a reproducible standalone SME GEMM with tier-A-style methodology vs Accelerate, LIBXSMM, KleidiAI and OpenBLAS; consider adding it as its own entry. The same author has an OpenBLAS SME2 PR (OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS#6072, not opened).
